_comment: The follow camera (refit phase 2; re-derived for the HD view, docs/plan-hd.md). World units, seconds and per-second rates. The view is data/display.json's view_w x view_h (308x184); a boss arena pulls it back to the whole 400x240 cell.
_lead: How far ahead of her centre the view looks, in the way she faces. Was 24 in a 400 view (she saw 224 ahead, 176 behind). The 308 view loses 46 on each side; 32 gives 8 of that back ahead (186 ahead, 122 behind, still over 7 tiles), and stays under a quarter of the view so a turn swings the camera 64, not a third of the screen.
_rates: Follow rates are per second and independent of the view's size: they say how quickly the camera catches up, not how far it can see. Unchanged.
_air_band: The vertical anchor band is a jump's height above the floor she stood on (a human jump peaks about 44 above it), not a fraction of the view. Unchanged; still inside half the view less the keep-in (92 - 32 = 60 > 56).
_look_y: The vertical look-ahead (HD pass; CameraMath.look_mode/climb_time/blend_look). The 184 view left a long fall ~37 below her centre (92 less the 55 lag at 330/s with follow_y_rate 6) and a sustained climb pinned at the keep-in edge, and the tape audit counted those landings blind. While it is on, the view centres look_y_ahead_px past her in the direction she is going PLUS her follow lag (smoothed speed / follow_y_rate), so at a steady speed the lag cancels and she sits on the upper third line on a fall (184/3 = 61 from the top, 31 above the centre: 30) with 92 + 30 - 10 = 112 units, 7 tiles, under her feet in view; on a climb the same on the lower third. The lag lead is capped at look_y_max_lag_px: the fastest fall is 340/6 = 57, so 60.
_look_fall: When a fall counts: faster than look_fall_speed (a third of the human's 330 max fall, reached 0.16 s past the apex) AND more than look_fall_drop_px below the floor she last stood on. Measured from the floor, so a jump that lands where it left never qualifies, and 52 is past a 3-tile step-down (48): only drops of 4 tiles and more lead the view.
_look_climb: When a climb counts: she has risen faster than look_climb_speed for look_climb_s on a leaky clock that drains look_climb_decay times as fast while she is not rising and empties when she stands. 40 is under a vine climb (60) and under the slowest point of a flapping bird's rise (172 - 420 x 0.24 = 71). The longest ordinary rise is the frog's jump, above 40/s for (340 - 40)/700 = 0.43 s (the human's is 0.29 s, a single bird flap 0.31 s), so 0.6 never fires on a jump but does on a vine after 0.6 s, a bird on its third flap in a row, a thermal, and a frog wall climb on its second hop (each wall jump rises 0.38 s and the cling between drains it at the same 1x, so a hop banks ~0.2 s). Every ordinary jump ends standing, which empties the clock, so the decay only ever acts in the air.
_look_rates: Per-second approach rates. The weight eases in at look_y_in_rate (63% in 0.125 s: a long fall is over in under a second, see _look_follow) and back out, on landing or turning round, at the gentler look_y_out_rate. look_y_vel_rate smooths the speed the lag lead reads, so a landing's sudden stop does not jerk the goal by the whole lag lead. The view step stays under the audit's 12/frame on every tape (tests/integration/tape_replay.gd).
_look_follow: While the look leads, the vertical follow runs at look_follow_y_rate instead of follow_y_rate (blended by the weight). A long fall is short: the tapes' worst (jungle_2, 216 below the take-off view) lasts about 0.8 s, and at rate 6 the view is still catching up when she lands. Modelled frame by frame on that fall (rate in 3/follow 6 -> 8/12, under follow_y_max_speed): the landing spot is in view 11 -> 14 frames before touch-down (4 with no look), the view step held at 8 a frame. The tape audit measures the real thing ([blind_lead] in the itest log). The lag lead is computed with the same blended rate, so where she settles is unchanged.
_follow_y_max: The vertical follow never scrolls faster than this (CameraMath.limit_step); keep_in still drags the view along with anything faster, so it can slow the view but never lose her. Needed because the look's quicker follow, switching on under a bird riding a thermal, stepped the view 15 a frame on heights_1 (the audit's bound is 12). 480/s is 8 a frame: past the fastest fall (340, 5.7 a frame) by enough to get ahead of it, and with the 108/s run across (1.8 a frame) still 8.2 a frame on the diagonal.
_keep_in: The hard zone: however fast she moves, her centre stays at least this far inside the view's edges (the smoothing alone let a thermal carry her out of frame). Was 64 x 40 of 400 x 240, 16% of each dimension; scaled to the 308 x 184 view that is 49 x 31, rounded to whole tiles: 48 (3 tiles) x 32 (2 tiles).
_wake: Ordinary enemies (src/enemies/wake_rule.gd): a despawned enemy respawns when its spawn comes within the view grown by enemy_wake_margin_px; an awake one despawns once its body is further out than enemy_sleep_margin_px. Both are distances past the view's edge, not fractions of it: the wake margin is what the view can scroll in the frames an enemy needs to be moving before it shows (the fastest follow is a fall, ~5.7 a frame, so 32 is ~6 frames), and the sleep margin is how far a chaser may step out of frame and still come back. Unchanged; tests/integration/tape_replay.gd audits both against the new view on every tape.
_arena: Boss arenas: the camera locks when Kaya's centre enters the arena, eases into it over arena_ease_s, and lets go once she is arena_release_px clear of it. The pull-back to the whole arena, and back in after, runs over the same arena_ease_s.
